answer: Autonomous barges bid for berth slots at a wharf where they unload copper concentrate. A bid counts only when its barge physically docks. Wave gauges on the pilings record the ripple each hull pushes against the wharf, and a crane scale weighs the copper it lands. If several identities claim the same berthing window but the gauges record a single ripple and the scale one load, the extra identities are fake and their bids are voided. Faking more barges would require more real hulls and cargo.
